newsitem.title: FRANCE: French court fines cigarette makers over labels.
newsitem.headline: French court fines cigarette makers over labels.

text.p: A Paris court has fined top executives of tobacco companies Seita and Rothmans after finding that health warnings printed on their cigarette packages distorted the meaning of the labeling law.

Seita, which makes the pungent Gauloises and Gitanes cigarettes and distributes other brands in France including Rothmans, said on Wednesday it would appeal against the ruling, which was issued on Monday.
The decision centred on mandatory health warnings on cigarette packages, which state: "Smoking is bad for your health".
Acting on a complaint by the National Committee against Tobacco Use. the court faulted the two firms for preceding the warning with the words, "According to Law No. 91-32..."

The court said the words additional "held the (health message) up to ridicule" by suggesting that only the law supported the conclusion that cigarettes were bad for health and not years of scientific research.

The court ordered Seita chairman Jean-Dominique Comolli to pay 300,000 francs ($52,000) in fines and damages. The top executives of Rothmans Europe, Rothmans Services and Rothmans Manufacturing were ordered to collectively ay another 200,000 francs ($35,000) in fines and damages.
A similar complaint is pending against Philip Morris Cos Inc, with a hearing set for September.
